note: Yearly events for the Draft Table. `roles`: the kind of neighbourhood it is held in, when it has one.

events.summary: Ploughmen drag a ribboned plough through the streets, begging pennies for the plough light and threatening to plough up the doorstep of anyone who won't give.
Everyone carries candles in procession to be blessed for the year, and the old folk watch the weather to know how long winter will last.
The whole town plays one game of football through the streets, upper end against lower, with no rules anyone admits to and shutters on every window.
Quarter day, when rents fall due, servants change places and everyone owes someone something.
After the long fast, the Easter fair brings eggs, lamb, dancing and travelling players to the market place.
Young people go maying in the woods at dawn and bring back green branches; the maypole goes up and a May queen is crowned.
The priest leads the parish round its boundaries, and the boys are bumped against each boundary stone so they never forget where it is.
Bonfires on every hill and at every street corner, people leaping through the flames for luck and staying up to see the sun rise.
Merchants from the coast come to buy the clip, and the town is full of fleeces, haggling and foreign money for a week.
Loaf-mass: the first bread from the new harvest is blessed, and the common fields are thrown open for grazing.
The last cart of the harvest is brought in with singing, and the farmers give a feast that ends in the barn with fiddles.
Quarter day and the goose fair: flocks of geese walked in from the villages, roast goose for dinner and the hiring fair for servants.
Bells rung for the dead, soul cakes given to children who go souling door to door, and candles left in the churchyard.
The beasts that cannot be fed through winter are killed and salted, and there is fresh meat for a feast before the lean months.
Twelve days of feasting, the Lord of Misrule, mummers' plays door to door and the Yule log burning in every hall.
Knights come from across the land for the lord's tournament: jousting in the lists, a melee, a feast and the whole town in the stands.
Paper lanterns set floating on the water for the spirits, and an old enchantment makes them drift upstream.
The day the last dragon was driven off, with a paper dragon chased through the streets by children with wooden swords.
On the shortest night the elves open their gardens to the town, and nobody quite remembers getting home.
The priest blesses the fishing boats in the harbour, decked with flowers, before the season begins.
The guilds act out the whole story of the world on carts through the streets, from Creation to Doomsday, in one long day.
Gentlemen pay New Year calls on every household they know, and the ladies keep count of who came.
The grandest night of the year at the Assembly Rooms, with a quadrille, a supper and the town's gossip for the rest of the winter.
Housewives race through the streets tossing pancakes in frying pans, cheered on by their husbands.
A bank holiday of races, a cricket match and the brass band in the park.
Sunday schools walk the town behind their banners and brass bands, children in new clothes collecting pennies.
The mills shut for a week and half the town goes to the seaside together, the other half stays and has the fair.
Rowing races, sailing races, a greasy pole and fireworks over the water, with the whole town on the banks.
Prize bulls, giant marrows, sheepdog trials and a beer tent, the farmers in town in their Sunday best.
Churches and chapels piled with sheaves, loaves and vegetables, then given to the poor and the hospital.
Every street builds its bonfire and burns its guy, with parkin, toffee and rockets fired at the next street's pile.
The Theatre Royal's pantomime, a dame, a principal boy and a transformation scene the whole town talks about.
A summer exhibition of the latest machines, with a glass pavilion, demonstrations and crowds from three counties.
Crowds gather at the field to watch the mail airship come back from her winter overhaul and take the first bags of the year.
Inventors race steam carriages, walking engines and flying machines across the moor, and most of them make it home.
A parade down Main Street, a speech, a barbecue, horse races, a dance and fireworks, and fights after.
Cowhands from every ranch gather the cattle for branding, then ride into town with their pay.
Bronc riding, steer roping and a county fair, with ranchers in from a hundred miles and every hotel room taken.
The old town's fiesta: a procession, a dance on the plaza, music, food and a cockfight nobody officially attends.
The anniversary of the first train, with a band at the depot, speeches about progress and free rides to the next town.
Church in the morning, turkey or whatever can be had, and a dance at the hall in the evening.
Firecrackers, a dragon dance down Main Street and an open house where everyone in town is welcome.

names: New Year's Eve at the Club
events.summary: Every club, hotel and speakeasy in town packed for New Year's Eve, and the police mostly looking the other way.
Ice skating on the pond, a toboggan run, an ice palace and a carnival queen.
Everyone in new hats strolling up the avenue after church, showing off, and photographers from the paper.
The ballclub's first home game, the mayor throws out the first pitch and the whole town finds a reason to leave work early.
Parades of old soldiers, wreaths on the graves and the band playing at the cemetery, then the first picnic of summer.
Parade, band concert, sack races, a clambake or barbecue and fireworks over the water.
A pageant on the boardwalk that scandalises the ministers and brings in visitors from across the state.
The Italian parish carries its saint through the streets pinned with dollar bills, with a street fair, sausages and fireworks.
Livestock, pie contests, a midway, harness racing and a barnstormer flying loops over the grandstand.
The unions parade with their banners, then picnics, a ball game and the last swim of summer.
The college football homecoming, a bonfire, a parade of floats and alumni in raccoon coats.
Children in sheets and masks, pranks on every porch and a party with bobbing for apples at the church hall.
Two minutes' silence at eleven o'clock, the veterans' parade to the memorial and the names read out.
The department stores unveil their Christmas windows, mechanical elves and toy trains, with crowds on the sidewalk.
Couples dancing for days for a cash prize, the crowd buying tickets to watch them stagger.
The fishing boats decked with flags parade past the priest on the pier, with wreaths thrown for the lost.
The bands of every club play the park, ending with a cutting contest that goes on past midnight.
Live music in every venue downtown, ice sculptures, a countdown and fireworks over the water at midnight.
Every restaurant in town does a cheap set menu for two weeks, and everybody books somewhere they normally can't afford.
A weekend of ice sculptures, a chili cook-off, a polar plunge for charity and a lot of hot cider.
Pipe bands, green beer, a parade down Main Street and the bars full by noon.
The minor league season opens with fireworks, hot dogs and the whole town in the stands.
Volunteers clean up the parks and the shore, then a festival with music and food trucks.
The trees in the park bloom and the town turns out for picnics, a 5K and a craft fair.
A Pride parade and street festival downtown, a drag brunch and rainbow flags on every shop.
A parade in the morning, cookouts all day and fireworks over the harbor or the ballpark at night.
Free concerts in the park every Thursday evening, people bringing blankets, wine and their dogs.
A weekend on the waterfront of lobster rolls, chowder contests, boat parades and a crowd from three states.
Main Street closed to cars for a weekend of food stalls, local bands, a bouncy castle and the mural festival.
Rides, fried everything, a demolition derby and the 4-H barns, with ribbons for the biggest pumpkin.
The college students come back, the streets fill up again and every bar has a welcome-back night.
Pick-your-own at the orchards, cider donuts, hay rides and a pie contest the same family always wins.
The breweries' Oktoberfest, polka bands, pretzels and a stein-holding contest nobody wins with dignity.
Trick-or-treating downtown, a costume parade, a haunted house in the old mill and pumpkins on every step.
The town's big run, half the town running and the other half cheering with signs.
The tree on the green lit up, carolers, a visit from Santa and hot chocolate for everyone.
A lion dance through the streets, firecrackers and restaurants packed for family banquets.
A week of independent films at the old theater, directors' talks and a closing party.
The anniversary of the launch: the founders' names read out, a feast in the commons and a toast to the people who left Earth.
The day the ship passes the halfway mark of the year's course, a festival of paper stars and children staying up late.
The growing decks' harvest festival: the first fruit of the cycle shared out, a dance among the crops and a prize for the oddest vegetable.
The lights are dimmed and the screens show Earth's skies, rain and seas all night, and people tell stories about the old world.
A week of dimmed lights and candles for midwinter, the way the founders kept it, ending with every light on at once.
When the ship docks for trade: new faces, new goods, crews on shore leave and the promenade open all night.
The academy's games: zero-g ball, drone races, a science fair and the whole ship cheering for its deck.
The names of everyone lost on the journey are read out in the memorial garden, and their families plant something green.
Paper lanterns hung along every corridor and the arboretum, for the new year, with dumplings and wishes.
The archive puts its paper books and Earth objects on show, and the academy reads old poems aloud.
Every adult votes for the ship's council; debates in the commons, campaign posters and a lot of strong opinions.
The engineers open the drive gallery for a day, and every child aboard gets to see the core glow.
The orchard decks blossom on schedule and people come with blankets to sit under the trees.
The anniversary of the first landing, with a parade from the old landing site and fireworks over the towers.
The spaceport's big launches, with crowds on the viewing galleries and the whole city looking up.
The day the sea wall was finished: a walk along the top, wreaths for the old drowned town and music on the promenade.
The Strip's festival of lights, every sign and hologram on the avenue redesigned for a week.
Once a year the seed vault is opened and seeds planted to keep them alive, each family planting one row.
The children act out the story of the founding in the amphitheatre, the same play every year with new jokes.
A day when anybody brings anything broken to the promenade and the fixers mend it for free.
The observatory opens to everyone for a night of telescopes, star charts and the destination star pointed out.
